name: Ladder: Registration response
summary: The registration rung, both halves. The CLIENT speaks first with RegistrationRequestV3Msg (wire 0x13, 2,750 bytes) carrying its version as a keyed string map; the server answers with RegistrationResponseMsg (wire 0x3, 88 bytes) carrying its own version as one dotted string. This moves the client from WaitingForREPConnection (14) to WaitingForActorGameConnection (15).
purpose: Exchange versions and accept the client's registration. The client sends its build first, so a private server's first job is to ANSWER that request, not to open the conversation.

created_when: the client has opened the REP connection and is waiting to register
lifecycle.if_absent: the client stays in WaitingForREPConnection and never reaches the actor game connection

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): measured 00 01 03: the typed envelope plus the prefix varint 0x03, a one-byte varint because the value is below 0x80.

fields.name: request_version_map
fields.note: Inside RegistrationRequestV3Msg the client sends its version as repeated `<u32 big-endian key><u8 length><bytes>`. Measured on the 1.400 capture: key 1 = 'Javelin', key 2 = '1', key 3 = '400', key 4 = '6031', key 5 = '6004151', key 8 = 91 bytes beginning '[RETAIL]'. Read together that is product, major, minor, build, revision and channel, i.e. 1.400.6031.6004151. The record begins with a 16-byte datagram preamble (ff c4 4f f7 ...) because it is the first message of its datagram.

fields.name: unresolved_u32_at_0x03
fields.note: Zero on the measured record. No second signal for what it is. Big-endian inferred from the repo rule that fixed-width wire integers are big-endian; the endianness itself is not measured.

fields.name: unresolved_u8_at_0x07
fields.note: Measured 0x0b. Plausibly a count or a length, but nothing confirms which.

fields.name: unresolved_8_at_0x08
fields.note: Measured 88 8d 68 70 6c 41 5b 20. Not an id that appears anywhere else in the capture. Big-endian inferred from the repo rule that fixed-width wire integers are big-endian; the endianness itself is not measured.

fields.name: unresolved_ids_at_0x10
fields.note: 32 bytes, fully redacted in the published dump, so the original content is lost. Could be one 32-byte id or two 16-byte ids. The size (32) is stated, so the shape is carried as bytes(32); the meaning stays unknown. meanings.md 'The first typed exchange, measured'. (#216).

fields.name: server_version
fields.note: The 36-byte ASCII string '#[RETAIL].Javelin.1.365.6031.6006993', with no length prefix in front of it: its start is fixed and its length is fixed by the format. This is the server's version, and its shape matches the client's own version format exactly. The captured server reports 1.365.6031.6006993 because that capture was taken on build 1.365, so server and client agreed.

fields.name: trailing_flags
fields.note: Measured 01 00 00 01, the last four bytes of the record. Big-endian inferred from the repo rule that fixed-width wire integers are big-endian; the endianness itself is not measured.

evidence.ref: services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt record 0x1_T0x3_R.bin: 88 bytes, seq 0x1, direction R, type 0x3. Offsets sum exactly: 3 header + 4 + 1 + 8 + 32 + 36 string + 4 = 88

handler FUN_1464768a0, .pdata 0x1464768a0-0x146476a1d (381 bytes), vtable slot 0x148503e28, reached through the adjustor thunk 'add rcx,8; jmp' at 0x146476896. It logs 'GameConnectionWrapper: received registration response from REP', passes the message to a virtual setter labelled 'Server version' (slot +0x2d0), then reads the client's own version string through a getter and hands it to the setter at +0x110

two independent signals agree that this body carries a server version: the decompiled handler labels the setter 'Server version', and the captured 88-byte body literally contains a version string in the client's own format

third independent signal, added 2026-10-25 after the scan-wire-names.py fix: research/derived/wire-type-names.json now resolves slot 3 to RegistrationResponseMsg. That name was not available when the rung was identified, because the scanner had been unrunnable since private-client/ moved to the repo root

the version format is corroborated by reverse/builds/30fe6461.../corpus/meta.json, whose 'versions' field is ['[RETAIL].Javelin.1.460.6033.6024067'], the same #[RETAIL].Javelin.<version> shape with the client's own build numbers

record 0x0_T0x13_W.bin: 2,750 bytes, direction W, type 0x13. The keyed-string pattern `<u32 BE key><u8 len><bytes>` reproduces on five consecutive runs at 0x20, 0x29, 0x31, 0x37 and 0x43, and key 8 at 0x45 has length 0x5b = 91 starting '[RETAIL]'

research/derived/wire-type-names.json resolves slot 19 (0x13) to RegistrationRequestV3Msg, slot 2 to RegistrationRequestV2Msg, slot 1 to RegistrationRequestMsg and slot 3 to RegistrationResponseMsg, so the whole registration family is named on this build

the client does NOT require an exact version match: the capture's client reports 1.400.6031.6004151 through the request keys while the server's response says '#[RETAIL].Javelin.1.365.6031.6006993', a different minor and revision, and the client still advanced. A private server can therefore answer with its own version string rather than having to impersonate the official one

research/sessions/live_20261022_r1460_first/REPORT.md records the two transitions 100 ms apart: 'WaitingForREPConnection -> WaitingForActorGameConnection' at 08:27:55.006 and 'WaitingForActorGameConnection -> WaitingForSpawnPoint' at 08:27:55.105, which places this rung and the next one in the same tenth of a second

PREDICTION CONFIRMED on the real build, 2026-10-25. The ficha predicted a 1.460 client should be told #[RETAIL].Javelin.1.460.6033.6024067. The official 1.460 session's Game.log shows exactly that at 08:27:54.940: 'LogEnvironmentString: Server version: [RETAIL].Javelin.1.460.6033.6024067'. Server and client versions matched because both were 1.460, which is what the earlier 1.365 capture also showed

research/atlas/meanings.md 'The first typed exchange, measured' and 'The complete map': the server->client half is wire 0x3 RegistrationResponseMsg, an 88-byte record, moving state 14 WaitingForREPConnection to 15 WaitingForActorGameConnection; the client speaks first with the 0x13 request
